page: Microsoft Azure F4ads_v7 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Fadsv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 472 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

In benchmark evaluations, the single-core performance of the AMD EPYC processor is highly competitive. The stress-ng single-core CPU test and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the top tier, with gzip reaching 40.89 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also places in the top tier at 17.86 GB/sec. Multi-core and multi-threaded operations, such as the stress-ng multi-core test and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, perform within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only small block cached transfers reaching 853.2 GB/sec and large block uncached writes at 34.32 GB/sec.

This hardware configuration is suitable for workloads requiring strong single-threaded CPU performance combined with local storage capacity, such as lightweight database operations, web serving, and basic text or image processing. The 472 GB local disk supports applications requiring fast local scratch space. However, resource-intensive multi-threaded tasks and larger workloads face limitations. For example, while LLM text generation with a small 135M model achieves top-tier speeds of 340.4 tokens/sec, prompt processing with a medium 7B model drops to a weak tier at 30.43 tokens/sec. This indicates a clear tradeoff when attempting to run larger machine learning or data-dense workloads on this instance size.
description: The Microsoft Azure F4ads_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by a dedicated 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 4 physical cores and 4 threads. It features 16.0 GB of RAM and 472 GB of local storage, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Benchmark data highlights top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. While the instance delivers efficient text generation for small language models, prompt processing for medium models is weak, representing a clear performance tradeoff. This server is suited for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and database operations that benefit from strong single-threaded execution and local storage.
